name: Grist
subcategory: spreadsheet databases and operational data apps
tagline: Combine spreadsheet formulas with relational records in a small self-hosted workspace
verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Grist, combine spreadsheet formulas with relational records in a small self-hosted workspace. The hard boundary is mature formula engine, access rules, collaboration, integrations, and hosting, plus data model flexibility, collaboration, and integrations.
coreLoopDIY: Combine spreadsheet formulas with relational records in a small self-hosted workspace, provide grid, form, kanban, and filtered views, and expose a documented API.
whatYouLose: mature formula engine, access rules, collaboration, integrations, and hosting
moatNotes: data model flexibility, collaboration, and integrations
ongoingBurden: schema changes, formulas, permissions, imports, attachments, views, APIs, concurrency, backups, and migrations
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Grist because teams pay when a flexible database becomes a shared operational system with integrations and years of accumulated business logic. The recurring cost buys schema changes, formulas, permissions, imports, attachments, views, APIs, concurrency, backups, and migrations, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: NocoDB
priorArt.desc: Active open-source no-code database interface and Airtable alternative.

alternatives.name: Baserow Community
alternatives.desc: A friendlier database grid with relations and formulas; less spreadsheet-like, more app-builder-like.

alternatives.name: Grist
alternatives.desc: The actual product, self-hosted: formulas, relational records, forms, and views in one small workspace.

alternatives.name: Teable Community
alternatives.desc: Relational tables, formula fields, forms, and views in a tidy self-hosted grid.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Mathesar
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Excellent relational data editing, but no spreadsheet formula model, the feature that makes Grist Grist.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a small-team structured database DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Grist in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: combine spreadsheet formulas with relational records in a small self-hosted workspace, provide grid, form, kanban, and filtered views, and expose a documented API.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create workspaces, bases, tables, fields, records, attachments, relations, and saved views.
Support text, number, currency, date, boolean, select, formula-lite, and relation field types.
Build grid, form, kanban, and record-detail views from one canonical schema.
Add role-based permissions, optimistic concurrency checks, audit history, and trash restore.
Provide CSV import or export and a token-authenticated REST API generated from the schema.
Ship migrations, seed data, backups, health checks, and a schema export format.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out full spreadsheet formula compatibility.
Deliberately leave out hundreds of automations and integrations.
Deliberately leave out large-enterprise governance and vendor-managed scale.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
